title: Characterizing the unmet need and burden of disease in adult HPP patients in Germany treated with best supportive care
summary:
To date, a single therapy is approved for hypophosphatasia (HPP)—asfotase alfa—and its indication is limited to a specific patient subgroup.

This observational study is intended to generate additional insights into the burden of disease, care pathways, and health-related quality of life among HPP patients who are not treated with asfotase alfa. 

The evidence generated is expected to support optimal clinical management and decision-making for adult HPP patients in Germany and to characterize the unmet medical need associated with disease burden and reduced quality of life in this population.
conditions: Disorders of phosphorus metabolism and phosphatases

interventions.name: Multicenter, observational study integrating cross-sectional data collection with historical data from patient medical records. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Patients aged ≥ 18 year at time of signed informed consent (Male or Female)
2. Diagnosis of HPP:
- Diagnosis of HPP is documented in medical records and
- Two documented serum ALP activity results, at least 15 days apart, below the age- and sex-adjusted local laboratory normal range, obtained from medical records and
- Signs or symptoms of HPP and 
- One of the following criteria: Documented TNSALP gene variant or Plasma PLP above the upper limit of normal (ULN) at any time since symptom onset 
3. Treated with best supportive care (BSC)
4. Able and willing to participate in the study
5. Able to give written informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
1. Previous and/ or current treatment with asfotase alfa (as study medication or product)
2. Current participation and/or previous participation in an interventional clinical trial with a medicinal product for HPP
